implementation_options: N2+D3+T2+R3 — Selected: Domain-grouped direct navigation, progressive disclosure, a two-column ticket workbench, and staged rollout improve scanning and task focus without changing routes, APIs, or permissions.
N1 — Rejected: A reordered flat list preserves immediate discoverability but leaves an already large navigation set difficult to scan.
N3 — Deferred: Collapsible groups add hidden destinations, focus-management requirements, and persistent-state complexity before evidence that sidebar height is a real problem.
N4 — Rejected: Role/recent-use personalization is unsupported by usage evidence and would make navigation placement unstable.
P1 — Rejected: Tokens alone cannot correct inconsistent page hierarchy or duplicated summary information.
P2+page-family hybrid — Selected: A canonical anatomy with overview, register/library, record-detail, analytics, and settings variants provides consistency while retaining purpose-specific layout.
P3 — Rejected: Mandatory KPI rows and uniform page bodies would preserve low-value zeroes and create decorative content.
D1 — Rejected: Always-visible controls and metadata currently over-weight filters and secondary detail.
D2 — Rejected: Hiding most controls would damage discovery and frequent-agent speed.
T1 — Rejected: Spacing changes alone do not resolve ticket-detail competition between conversation, properties, audit, and AI.
T3 — Deferred: A tab-only record interface would fragment essential context; selective secondary views achieve the benefit with less risk.
R1 — Rejected: An app-wide rewrite has an unnecessarily broad authorization, responsive, and rollback surface.
R2 — Rejected: Independent cosmetic edits would recreate route-by-route drift.

# Tickety UI organization plan

## 1. Decision and guardrails

Adopt a grouped, always-expanded sidebar; a shared page-anatomy system; progressive disclosure for secondary controls; and a two-column ticket workbench on wide screens. Preserve the current dark branded shell, routes, role gates, demo restrictions, API/query contracts, and existing responsive table/card alternatives. This is an information-architecture migration, not a rebrand or feature expansion.

Observed facts are the supplied source and 1440×900 screenshot review. The hierarchy choices below are reversible product judgments made to prioritize frequent operational work over visual symmetry.

## 2. Global shell and navigation

Use the existing fixed desktop sidebar and mobile drawer. Replace the single flat `Workspace` list with visible, non-collapsible groups; every destination remains a direct link and retains its existing route, active state, and role gate.

| Group | Exact placement |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Dashboard |
| Work | Tickets, My Time |
| Service operations | Services, Problems, Changes, Assets |
| Knowledge and people | Knowledge Base, Agents, Surveys, Leaderboard |
| Insights | Reports, Intelligence |
| Account | Profile |
| Administration | Settings |

`Agents`, `Intelligence`, and `Settings` are rendered only when their current authorization rules allow them. Do not show a disabled destination that reveals protected capability. Keep Profile and Settings visually separated at the sidebar bottom; Settings stays bottom-most, and Profile precedes it. My Time moves into Work because it is an individual operational task, not an account preference.

Keep the desktop content max width, but give dense registers a documented `page--wide` variant within it. Mobile retains the sticky 64px top bar with an accessible menu trigger; opening the drawer traps focus, Escape closes it, route selection closes it, and the trigger receives focus on close. Group labels are headings, not links. No collapsible groups, personalization, command palette, favorites, or nav search in this phase.

## 3. Shared page anatomy and primitives

Create shared layout primitives by composing the existing Button, Badge, Alert, Dialog, EmptyState, ErrorState, Skeleton, SearchableSelect, and table/card responsive components; do not introduce an unrelated component system.

- `PageFrame`: consistent responsive gutters, page-width variant, and vertical rhythm.
- `PageHeader`: optional eyebrow, one consistent title type rule, optional short description, and right-aligned primary action(s). Use sans-serif titles throughout for operational clarity; this may be changed centrally later.
- `ContextAlertRegion`: immediately below the header, only for actionable warnings/errors; no empty reserved space.
- `ActionableSummary`: optional, concise metrics or status summary; show only values that change a decision or lead to a next action.
- `ContentToolbar`: search first, then visible frequent filters, then a labeled `More filters` control, sort, and view controls. Saved views live here, not in a separate full-width strip.
- `RegisterLayout` and `CardGridLayout`: shared table/card body, result count, loading/empty/error/partial-data treatment, and responsive switch.
- `DetailHero`, `ActivityPane`, `PropertiesRail`, and `SecondaryPanel`: reusable record-detail pieces.
- `Section`: title, optional one-line purpose, actions, body, and standard spacing; use it rather than route-local border/gap conventions.

Canonical sequence is: PageHeader → ContextAlertRegion → optional ActionableSummary → primary toolbar and primary content → secondary insight/help. Exceptions: record details retain a compact breadcrumb before DetailHero; analytics can put a time-range/filter toolbar before charts; settings use section navigation before configuration content. A summary is omitted when it only repeats a visible register count, contains zero-value metrics, or delays the primary task.

All controls must retain visible or programmatic labels, keyboard access, focus visibility, logical DOM order, live announcements for filtering/loading/results, and semantic headings/table relationships. Never make essential actions available only on hover, by color, or inside an unlabeled icon menu.

## 4. Page arrangements

### Dashboard

1. Header: `Dashboard`, current scope/time context, and only relevant global action.
2. Contextual warnings: sync, permission, or data-quality alerts only.
3. Operational Pulse: reduce to a compact actionable strip containing at most the three highest-priority indicators; each links to its filtered work. Remove values duplicated in the metric row.
4. Priority Queue: first major body region, above broad metrics; show the next actionable tickets with owner/status/SLA priority and a clear `View all tickets` path.
5. Supporting metrics: two-to-four decision-supporting cards, responsive grid; omit low-value/zero cards instead of filling slots.
6. Recommendation/insight panel: below work and metrics, visibly marked as advisory with loading/error/empty states.

### Ticket Queue

1. Header with `Tickets`, result context, primary `New ticket`, and secondary fetch/import action if currently permitted.
2. Context alerts.
3. Single compact ContentToolbar: search; visible high-frequency status/assignee filters; Saved Views as a select/control in the same row; `More filters` opens a labeled popover/drawer holding the remaining dropdowns; sort remains visible. Applied hidden filters show removable chips and a `Clear filters` action.
4. Result count plus responsive TicketList/table as the primary body. Preserve existing card alternative on narrow screens.
5. Empty state distinguishes no tickets from no filter results and offers safe clear-filter/create actions; error and partial-sync states preserve retry/recovery affordances.

Do not place an oversized filter card ahead of the register. Keep filter state in the existing URL/query behavior; close a mobile filter drawer only after an explicit Apply action, and restore focus to its trigger.

### Ticket Detail

1. Compact breadcrumb.
2. DetailHero: ticket identifier, concise title, status/priority badges, requester/customer context, and primary actions. Keep status-changing/closing actions explicit and retain current destructive confirmation.
3. Wide screens (≥1024px): `ActivityPane` left (about 2/3) and sticky `PropertiesRail` right (about 1/3). Conversation is the default activity and retains composer, attachments, and existing permission/error states. The rail starts with status, assignee, priority, SLA/due context, then remaining editable properties grouped by work relevance.
4. Secondary content: Intelligence and Audit are labeled secondary panels below the workbench or opened from clearly labeled in-page controls; they are not equal first-screen columns. AI guidance is advisory, keeps provenance/safety behavior, and does not obscure conversation or action controls.
5. Narrow screens: DetailHero → status/actions → Conversation → essential properties → expandable remaining properties → Intelligence → Audit. Keep the same DOM/task order; do not rely on visual reordering that confuses screen readers.

### Operational registers and libraries

Services, Problems, Changes, Assets, and Knowledge Base use `RegisterLayout` or `CardGridLayout`:

1. Header and route-specific create/import action where it already exists.
2. Actionable alert.
3. Optional summary of one-to-three nonredundant operational measures only.
4. Compact toolbar and result count.
5. Register/grid as the dominant region; use cards for existing mobile presentation or inherently visual/library content.
6. Secondary help or guidance last.

Services emphasize health/ownership before description; Problems emphasize impact/status and linked work; Changes emphasize risk/window/status; Assets emphasize lifecycle/owner/state; Knowledge emphasizes search, category, relevance, and article result. Avoid four mandatory count cards and eliminate zero/repeated counts.

### People and engagement

Agents is a people register: header/actions → operational alerts → compact workload/availability summary only if actionable → search/filter toolbar → agent list/cards. Put individual profile/workload detail inside the row/detail path, not a dashboard-like card wall.

Surveys is a work list: response/participation context only when it drives follow-up → filters → responses/campaign list → analysis/supporting insight. Leaderboard is an engagement overview: concise period selector and primary ranking first, then trends/recognition explanation; never let gamification panels displace operational work elsewhere.

### Analytics and administration

Reports: header with scope/time controls → data/sync warning → compact, nonduplicative KPI strip → primary decision charts → supporting breakdowns/tables. Preserve chart alternatives and expose data meaning in accessible text/table form.

Intelligence: header → availability/authorization/data-quality state → highest-confidence actionable findings ordered by urgency → evidence/provenance and recommended next action → lower-confidence or historical panels. Protected intelligence remains entirely role-gated; partial analysis is clearly labeled rather than represented as complete.

Settings: header → contextual security/integration warning → visible in-page section navigation (Account/workspace, integrations, notifications, security/access, data/demo as currently applicable) → one section at a time with Save/Cancel scoped to that section → destructive/integration actions last with existing confirmation. On desktop this may be a local side nav; on mobile it becomes an accessible select or horizontal section list. Keep unsaved-change warning and existing error recovery behavior.

## 5. Responsive and interaction rules

| Viewport | Arrangement |
| --- | --- |
| ≥1024px | Fixed grouped sidebar; header actions align right; toolbar stays one row when space permits; register tables; ticket two-column workbench with sticky rail. |
| 768–1023px | Sidebar remains only if current shell supports it comfortably, otherwise use drawer; toolbar wraps by control priority; tables may preserve horizontal scroll with a labeled scroll region or use existing cards; ticket rail becomes non-sticky below activity or a top summary followed by activity. |
| <768px | Sticky top bar and drawer; one-column pages; header actions wrap with primary action first; search full width, frequent filters next, `More filters` in drawer; cards replace dense tables where existing patterns support it; ticket sequence follows the explicit mobile order above. |

Use practical CSS container/viewport breakpoints but test at 320px, 375px, 768px, 1024px, and 1440px. Hidden secondary controls must remain reachable through labeled controls. Preserve URL state, browser back behavior, focus restoration, keyboard table/card actions, and touch targets.

## 6. Compatibility, failure paths, and safety

Maintain every existing role/access check at the route and action level; navigation grouping changes presentation only. Preserve demo-mode restrictions, safe external-link handling, API contracts, query parameters, optimistic/retry behavior, and realtime validation. Layout primitives must accept the current loading, error, empty, partial-data, and permission-denied states rather than replacing them with generic blank panels.

For every migrated route, test: initial skeleton; successful data; no data; no filter matches; API error and retry; partial/sync-degraded data; forbidden role; demo-restricted action; destructive action confirmation/cancel; keyboard-only navigation; screen-reader names/status announcements; and desktop/tablet/mobile layout. Ensure intelligence/AI error states expose recovery without leaking protected data or hiding the underlying ticket.

## 7. Phased delivery, verification, rollback, and stop conditions

### Phase 0 — baseline and contracts

Capture route screenshots and interaction checks at target widths; inventory existing route-level headers/toolbars/cards and current role/demo behavior. Define acceptance snapshots and accessibility checks before changing layout.

Stop if current route behavior cannot be characterized, if a shared primitive would require an API/permission change, or if the migration exposes an unresolved product-authority choice. Roll back by deleting only the baseline branch changes; no user-facing behavior changes ship here.

### Phase 1 — shell and primitives

Implement grouped Sidebar metadata and PageFrame/PageHeader/ContextAlertRegion/ContentToolbar/Section/RegisterLayout primitives while preserving existing route content. Migrate a low-risk register as the reference implementation.

Verify route/role matrix, keyboard drawer behavior, visual regression at target widths, and existing frontend tests. Roll back by retaining old route-local layout behind a temporary feature flag or reverting the primitive adoption commit; routing and data code remain untouched.

Stop before Phase 2 if navigation destinations become hidden, focus management fails, or a role/demo regression is found.

### Phase 2 — highest-frequency workflow

Migrate Dashboard, Ticket Queue, and Ticket Detail to the explicit arrangements above. Preserve current query strings and ticket actions; remove only demonstrably duplicated display values.

Verify ticket creation/edit/status/conversation/audit/AI paths, filter URL/back behavior, responsive sequence, loading/error/empty/partial states, and screen-reader landmarks. Roll back per route through a feature flag or isolated route-layout revert, without rolling back shared safe primitives.

Stop if primary ticket work cannot remain visible without losing a required control, if workflow tests regress, or if content truncation at required viewports blocks action.

### Phase 3 — operational and engagement families

Migrate Services, Problems, Changes, Assets, Knowledge Base, Agents, Surveys, and Leaderboard using the shared family patterns. Remove redundant metric rows only after comparing the information to the register body.

Verify each route's existing primary action, filters, cards/table behavior, role gate, and failure states. Roll back route-by-route.

### Phase 4 — analytics, settings, and polish

Migrate Reports, Intelligence, and Settings; finish responsive/accessibility consistency; remove transitional route-local CSS only after all migrations pass.

Verify protected intelligence, settings save/cancel/unsaved/destructive flows, chart alternatives, and no unauthorized navigation/action exposure. Roll back these routes independently; keep stable primitives.

Completion requires: all routes mapped to a named page family; no flat primary navigation list remains; the three critical pages match their specified order at tested breakpoints; no acceptance-path regression; no critical keyboard/screen-reader issue; no unauthorized/demo-restricted capability becomes reachable; and no duplicated low-value summary remains without a documented reason. If these cannot be met within the no-backend-change constraint, stop and retain the unshipped route at its prior layout.

## 8. Measurement and retained unknowns

Use reversible qualitative checks in this first rollout: time and clicks to reach Tickets/My Time and create/update a ticket, visibility of first actionable queue item at 1440×900 and mobile, toolbar discoverability, accessibility defect count, and route-level regression count. Do not claim a productivity improvement without later telemetry or research.

Retain for product research: dominant roles/workflows; compact versus comfortable density; whether My Time should remain globally visible; whether command palette/favorites/remembered filters earn their complexity; mobile usage and minimum viewport; and the durable serif-versus-sans title preference. None blocks the selected phased plan because each can be adjusted centrally or deferred.

## 9. Scope exclusions and risks

Excluded: code implementation in this task, backend/API/data-model changes, new routes/capabilities, public login/portal redesign, mockups, rebrand, permission redesign, and claims based on unavailable analytics.

Primary risks are over-normalizing route-specific work, hiding necessary controls through disclosure, mobile overflow, and accidental authorization regressions. Mitigate with declared page-family exceptions, visible frequent controls, breakpoint interaction tests, route/action authorization tests, feature-flagged route migration, and commit-level rollback boundaries.
